items.text: The system shall prevent Autopilot activation, or promptly limit and disengage it, when the vehicle is outside its defined operational domain, including on roads or in conditions where the system cannot safely perform its intended functions.

The system shall detect and respond safely to hazards in or entering the vehicle’s path, including crossing or turning vehicles, vehicles cutting in, motorcycles, and large vehicles, rather than relying only on lane markings or a vehicle ahead.
The system shall monitor whether the driver is attentive and able to resume control, not infer readiness solely from steering-wheel torque.
If the driver does not respond to escalating takeover alerts, the system shall execute a defined safe fallback maneuver that reduces risk without an abrupt or unexpected loss of control.

The system shall provide collision warning and emergency braking when required to avoid or mitigate an imminent collision, including when Autopilot is active or its steering or speed-control functions are unavailable.
The system shall detect sensor, processing, or actuator faults and degraded performance, notify the driver, and prevent continued operation that depends on unreliable functions.
The system shall detect when lane information is missing, ambiguous, or inconsistent and shall not continue steering on an unsupported assumption about the lane or road path.
The system shall maintain a safe following distance and respond safely to changes in that distance, including when another vehicle enters the gap.

The system shall clearly communicate when each automation function is active, unavailable, or disengaging, and shall make its limitations and any required driver action apparent in time for a safe response.
The system shall limit speed and automated operation to values and conditions for which it can maintain safe control, accounting for road geometry, visibility, and available traction.

stages.prompt:
You are a requirements engineer reviewing a safety-critical system.

Read the system description below. List the 10 most important requirements that are missing from it:
things the system should do or guarantee for safe operation that the description does not cover.
Give at most 10, ranked from most to least important.

Reply with JSON only, in this shape:
{"requirements": [{"text": "The system shall ..."}]}

System description:
# Case: Tesla Model S with Autopilot (Williston, Florida, 2016)

Source: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-17/02. This is a description of the system and its use before the crash. It does not include the investigation findings.

## System
A 2015 Tesla Model S has Autopilot, a SAE Level 2 partial driving automation feature. It combines Traffic-Aware Cruise Control (TACC) and Autosteer (lane keeping). The driver stays responsible for driving and monitoring the road.

## Main parts
- Sensors: a forward-facing camera, a forward-facing radar and ultrasonic sensors.
- Vision processing: a camera-based system detects lane markings and objects ahead.
- TACC: holds a speed set by the driver, slows down for a vehicle ahead in the same lane, and speeds up again when the lane is clear.
- Autosteer: keeps the vehicle centered in its lane using lane markings and the vehicle ahead.
- Forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking are available as separate features.
- Driver monitoring: the system checks that the driver's hands are on the steering wheel by sensing steering torque, and shows visual and audible alerts if no hands are detected for a period of time.

## People
- The driver sets the cruising speed, turns Autopilot on, and is told to keep hands on the wheel and watch the road.
- Other road users include cars, large trucks crossing or joining the road, and motorcyclists.

## Operating context
Autopilot is intended mainly for highways with limited access, in good visibility. Drivers can also turn it on for other roads, such as divided highways with cross traffic at intersections.
